trust_decision.summary: Whether a request header whose name is an underscore (or mixed-case) variant of a header Traefik manages may reach the backend is decided once per entry point, in the outermost HTTP handler wrapper built by createHTTPServer, from a static-config value that defaults to keep; the auth middlewares themselves keep managing only the canonical dash form.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names BasicAuth / DigestAuth / ForwardAuth and the published docs call out ForwardAuth authResponseHeaders by name, so an engineer opens forwardAuth and sees req.Header.Del(http.CanonicalHeaderKey(headerName)) followed by a dash-keyed write, which never touches X_Auth_User.

fix_sites.entry_point: entry point defaults, including the implicit http and traefik entry points created in SetEffectiveConfiguration
every configured TCP/HTTP entry point (plain HTTP, h2c, HTTPS, HTTP/3) built by NewTCPEntryPoint
same entry points, via the two new request-header handlers wrapped around the router

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The published fix is a documented opt-in: keep is the default and the docs say existing behaviour is preserved, so a solver can argue the auth middlewares must not be changed and that routes reached only through the middleware (headerField, authResponseHeadersRegex, customRequestHeaders) are the operator's responsibility for not setting delete/reject.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Underscore header names are legal and are set on purpose by operators (customRequestHeaders accepts any header name, and backends may legitimately consume X_Custom_Header); an over-broad change that strips or 400s every underscore header unconditionally, instead of behind a keep-by-default strategy, breaks those deployments and the documented back-compatible default.

O6_input_shapes: canonical dash form X-Auth-User (must keep working)
underscore at any position, including the first and last character (Contains, not prefix/suffix)
unset or empty strategy treated as keep
invalid strategy value rejected at server construction
request trailers (claimed in the new handlers' comments, not implemented)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: basicAuth headerField: the authenticated user is written under the dash key only, so a client-supplied underscore variant of the same header survives to the backend
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: headerField is marked deprecated (the in-code TODO says the canonical key should be added) and the report's example is ForwardAuth, so it reads as out of date rather than in scope
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the landing point (pkg/middlewares/auth)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: digestAuth headerField: same dash-only Del+Set of the user header on successful authentication
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: digest auth is rarely fronted by CGI-style backends, and the advisory's example names ForwardAuth authResponseHeaders
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the landing point (pkg/middlewares/auth)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: forwardAuth authResponseHeadersRegex: keys are matched against an operator regex written for the dash form, so an underscore variant is neither deleted from the request nor replaced
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the operator authors the regex, so the argument goes that they could write [_-] themselves; the explicit-list path is the documented, supported case
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the landing point, different option in the same handler

O8_uncovered_routes.route: headers customRequestHeaders with an empty value intends to remove a client-supplied header, but req.Header.Del removes only the dash key, so an underscore variant is forwarded
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: customRequestHeaders is a general-purpose rewriting feature, not an authentication control, so it is plausibly argued to be outside an advisory about auth middlewares; it also sits in a different package from where the report leads
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (pkg/middlewares/headers), one level away from pkg/middlewares/auth, and not mentioned anywhere in the advisory summary

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Extend isManagedXHeader-style underscore-tolerant identity to every managed header, not just the X-Forwarded-* set
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This helper already exists at the pinned commit as the earlier cohort's fix, so a maintainer fixing the auth side would naturally copy or generalise it instead of adding an entry point option

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second managed-header list (for example a new authResponseHeaders variant) that deletes and rewrites the configured names through the same dash-only Del+write
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already has a legacy and a new writeHeader variant side by side, so adding one more managed-header path with the same shape is an ordinary change here

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A header-deletion path for operator-configured names that must also match underscore variants
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The empty-value-means-delete convention is already the documented way to strip a client header, and the same three-line loop appears in the auth middlewares

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third entry-point level request-header wrapper next to encodeQuerySemicolons/normalizePath/sanitizePath/denyFragment, e.g. for response headers or for connection-level headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The chain is a flat list of small wrappers with one option each, so a maintainer adding a sibling sanitizer here is the established pattern

O9_family: authentication/identity spoofing through a header-name canonicalization differential (dash vs underscore vs case), CWE-178/CWE-290/CWE-345
